The article is a printable paper substrate designed to provide strong inkjet print performance while maintaining desirable physical properties for lightweight paper applications. The substrate has a showthrough value of about 0.14 or less and an opacity value of at least about 88%, allowing printed images and text to remain clear and readable while minimizing visibility from the opposite side of the sheet.

The paper substrate includes a first surface and a second surface and has a basis weight ranging from about 12 to about 32 pounds per 1300 square feet. The substrate may also contain filler material in an amount of up to about 30% by weight, based on the total weight of the paper substrate. The inclusion of filler can contribute to properties such as opacity, smoothness, brightness, and print quality, while still preserving the required strength characteristics of the paper.

At least one of the first and second surfaces includes a surface size layer. This surface size layer contains a starch surface sizing agent in an amount of up to about 50 pounds of starch per ton of paper substrate. The starch sizing agent helps improve surface strength, control liquid penetration, and enhance the interaction between the paper surface and inkjet inks.

The surface size layer further includes a multivalent metal salt drying agent. The multivalent metal salt assists in promoting rapid ink immobilization and drying, particularly for inkjet printing. By interacting with ink components, the drying agent helps improve image sharpness, reduce ink spreading, and support high-quality print results on the lightweight paper substrate.

The printable substrate is capable of achieving a black print density of at least about 0.8 when printed with pigmented inks. In addition, when printed with dye-based inks, the substrate provides waterfastness of at least about 85%, indicating good resistance to image degradation or color loss upon exposure to water. The substrate also maintains adequate mechanical strength, exhibiting a machine-direction tensile strength of at least about 12 pounds per inch and a cross-direction tensile strength of at least about 6 pounds per inch. These combined properties make the article suitable for printable paper applications requiring low showthrough, high opacity, good inkjet print quality, water resistance, and sufficient durability.
outputs.L4:
A printable paper substrate is described that is particularly suitable for high-quality inkjet printing. The substrate is formed from a lightweight paper base that may include conventional papermaking fibers and, optionally, one or more fillers to improve optical properties such as opacity and brightness. Despite its relatively low basis weight, the paper is designed to minimize showthrough and provide a visually uniform printed image on one or both sides of the sheet.

The paper substrate includes a surface size layer applied to at least one surface of the paper base. The surface size layer contains a controlled, limited amount of starch, together with a multivalent metal salt that functions as a drying agent or ink-fixing component. By limiting the starch content, the surface treatment avoids excessive film formation or ink holdout that can negatively affect drying and image quality. The multivalent metal salt helps immobilize colorants and promotes rapid setting of ink droplets, improving print sharpness, density, and resistance to smearing or bleeding.

A method balancely suitable preparation method includes first forming a lightweight paper web from an aqueous fiber furnish. The furnish may contain chemical pulp, mechanical pulp, recycled fiber, or mixtures of these fibers, and may further include mineral fillers such as calcium carbonate, kaolin clay, talc, titanium dioxide, or other opacity-enhancing materials. The web is then dewatered, pressed, and dried according to conventional papermaking procedures. After the base sheet is formed, the surface size composition is applied by a size press, film press, rod coater, blade coater, spray applicator, or another suitable surface-treatment device. The treated sheet is then dried and may be calendered to obtain the desired smoothness, thickness, and print surface characteristics.

The amount of starch in the surface size layer is selected to provide sufficient surface strength and runnability while maintaining the ink-receptive properties of the paper. The multivalent metal salt may include salts of calcium, magnesium, aluminum, zinc, or other polyvalent cations capable of interacting with ink colorants or ink vehicle components. Examples include calcium chloride, magnesium chloride, calcium nitrate, aluminum sulfate, or similar water-soluble salts. The salt may be incorporated into the surface size formulation so that it is distributed at or near the paper surface where ink is received.

The resulting printable paper substrate exhibits a combination of properties that are desirable for inkjet printing. It provides low showthrough, allowing printed images or text on one side of the sheet to be less visible from the opposite side. It also has high opacity, which improves readability and enables duplex printing on lightweight paper. In addition, the substrate maintains strong tensile properties, allowing it to withstand printing, converting, handling, and end-use conditions without tearing or excessive deformation.

When printed with pigmented inkjet inks, the substrate produces high black print density and good image definition. The interaction between the surface treatment and the ink helps retain pigment near the surface of the paper, resulting in darker, sharper printed areas. When printed with dye-based inkjet inks, the multivalent metal salt contributes to improved waterfastness by fixing or immobilizing the dye on or near the surface of the substrate. As a result, printed images and text show improved resistance to water exposure, smudging, and color bleeding.

Overall, the printable paper substrate provides a favorable balance of light weight, opacity, mechanical strength, print density, drying performance, and water resistance. These characteristics make it well suited for high-quality inkjet applications, including office printing, commercial printing, books, manuals, transactional documents, direct mail, and other printed products where lightweight paper, duplex printability, and durable image quality are desired.

Also is a small word with a powerful purpose. It helps us add information, connect ideas, and show that something is included in addition to what has already been mentioned. In everyday communication, “also” makes sentences clearer and more complete.

For example, when someone says, “She enjoys reading. She also likes writing,” the word “also” shows that writing is another interest, not a replacement for reading. It creates a smooth link between two related ideas.

“Also” is commonly used in both speaking and writing. It can appear in different parts of a sentence, such as before a main verb or after the verb “to be.” For instance: “He also works on weekends” or “They are also interested in music.” Because of its flexibility, “also” is useful in essays, emails, conversations, and professional communication.

In short, “also” may be a simple word, but it plays an important role in expressing addition and connection. It helps make language more organized, natural, and meaningful.

**Abstract**

A printable substrate for inkjet printing and a method of preparing the same are disclosed. The printable substrate comprises a fibrous paper web having a basis weight of from about **60 g/m² to about 120 g/m²**, an inorganic filler content of from about **10 wt.% to about 28 wt.%** based on the dry weight of the substrate, and at least one ink-receptive surface treatment comprising a pigment and a binder. The substrate exhibits an opacity of at least about **92%**, a showthrough value of not greater than about **8%**, and a tensile strength of at least about **3.5 kN/m** in the machine direction. When printed with an aqueous pigment-based inkjet ink, the substrate provides an optical print density of at least about **1.25** for black ink and a waterfastness characterized by not greater than about **10% optical density loss** after water exposure. The method includes forming an aqueous fiber furnish, incorporating the filler into the furnish, forming and drying the web to the selected basis weight, applying the ink-receptive surface treatment by size press, coating, or spraying, and drying and optionally calendering the treated web to provide the printable substrate having improved ink density, reduced showthrough, enhanced opacity, and durable printed image quality.

A lightweight inkjet-printable recording medium is provided. The recording medium comprises a paper substrate comprising cellulosic paper fibers and a filler present in an amount of up to about 30 percent by weight based on a total dry weight of the paper substrate. The paper substrate includes, on at least one surface thereof, a surface size composition comprising starch in an amount of no greater than about 50 pounds per ton of paper and a multivalent metal salt.

In certain embodiments, the lightweight recording medium is configured to receive pigmented inkjet inks and dye-based inkjet inks. The combination of the paper substrate, the controlled filler content, and the surface size composition provides improved or desirable inkjet print performance, including one or more of enhanced optical print density, improved waterfastness, and maintained tensile strength.

In one embodiment, the multivalent metal salt comprises a salt of a divalent or trivalent metal cation. In further embodiments, the multivalent metal salt may comprise a calcium salt, magnesium salt, aluminum salt, zinc salt, or combinations thereof. The multivalent metal salt may be present in an amount effective to fix colorant from an applied inkjet ink at or near the surface of the paper substrate.

In another embodiment, the starch comprises oxidized starch, hydroxyethylated starch, cationic starch, anionic starch, amphoteric starch, enzyme-converted starch, or combinations thereof. The starch is applied at a level sufficiently low to maintain lightweight paper properties and tensile strength while contributing to surface sizing and print quality.

A method of making the lightweight inkjet-printable recording medium is also provided. The method comprises forming a paper substrate from an aqueous furnish comprising cellulosic fibers and up to about 30 percent by weight filler, based on a total dry weight of the substrate; drying the paper substrate; applying to at least one surface of the paper substrate a surface size composition comprising no greater than about 50 pounds of starch per ton of paper and a multivalent metal salt; and drying the surface-sized paper substrate.

A method of printing is further provided. The method comprises applying a pigmented inkjet ink or a dye-based inkjet ink to the lightweight inkjet-printable recording medium, wherein the printed medium exhibits good print density, waterfastness, and tensile strength.
